cases.title: 鸟类起源：理论提出、反驳与新证据

paragraphs.text: The 'birds are dinosaurs' theory was first developed by English palaeontologist Thomas Huxley (1825–1895). According to some accounts, one evening Huxley went to dinner still thinking about a mystery dinosaur bone in his lab. He knew he was dealing with the lower leg bone (tibia) of a meat-eating, two-legged dinosaur belonging to the classification known as theropods, but attached to the tibia was an unidentified extra bone. On the menu that evening was quail, a small bird similar to a pheasant, and Huxley noticed the same strange bone, attached to the quail tibia on his plate. He later realised that it was in fact the bird's anklebone. More importantly, Huxley concluded that its forms in both dinosaur and bird skeletons were so similar that they must be closely related.

Huxley's idea fell out of favour for fifty years following the 1916 publication of The Origin of Birds by the Danish doctor Gerhard Heilmann. During this time, Heilmann’s theory was widely accepted. Heilmann had noted that two-legged, meat-eating dinosaurs lacked collarbones. In later evolutionary stages these bones fuse together to form the distinctive 'Y'-shaped bone in a bird's neck, known as the furcula. Heilmann proposed the notion that such a feature could not be lost and then re-evolve at a later date, so dinosaurs could not be the ancestors of birds.

Then, in the late 1960s, John Ostrom from Yale University in the USA, noted 22 features in the skeletons of meat-eating dinosaurs that were also found in birds and nowhere else. This reset the thinking on bird ancestry and once again Huxley’s ideas caught the attention of the scientific community. Subsequent work has found up to 85 characteristics that tie dinosaurs and birds together. But what of Heilmann's missing bones? It turns out that not only did many dinosaurs have collarbones, these were also fused together into a furcula. Unfortunately for Heilmann, the fossil evidence was somewhat lacking in his day, and the few furculae that had been found were misidentified, usually as belly ribs.

questions.prompt: Huxley formulated his theory while studying a dinosaur belonging to a group called ________ .
questions.evidence: a meat-eating, two-legged dinosaur belonging to the classification known as theropods
questions.explanation: group called问分类，theropods是类别；tibia是腿骨，quail是鸟，都不是恐龙类别。

structure: 三段按提出关联、否定关联、重新评价的顺序讲述鸟类与恐龙关系研究的变化。变化的关键是骨骼证据的解释，而不是简单的“旧学者对、新学者错”。阅读时要把当时的判断与后来材料所述发现区分开。
2：第2段叙述赫胥黎从恐龙腿骨与鹌鹑骨骼的相似处受到启发，并把额外骨骼认作踝骨。According to some accounts把晚餐故事标为一些记载中的说法。他据两类骨骼形态相近推断关系密切，段落重点是比较解剖结构怎样促成一个解释。
3：第3段交代赫胥黎的观点为何一度失去支持：海尔曼认为某类恐龙没有锁骨，又认为这种特征不可能消失后再次演化出现，于是排除了它们作为鸟类祖先的可能。这里是在解释他的论证前提，不是在把“恐龙没有锁骨”继续当作事实。
4：第4段呈现后来对共同特征的重新识别，以及更多相关骨骼证据。缺失锁骨的问题被重新解释为当时化石不足、已发现标本遭到误认。up to 85表示后续工作记录的数量上限式表述，不是说每种恐龙与每种鸟都有完全相同的85项特征。

cases.title: 鸟类起源：两方论点与过渡化石

source.title: IELTS Academic Reading official computer sample · The origins of birds
source.originalUnit: IELTS Academic Reading official computer sample · The origins of birds · 189731169

paragraphs.text: US ornithologist Alan Feduccia and palaeontologist Larry Martin are two vocal opponents of the dinosaur theory. They contend that birds evolved from some unknown reptile at a time long before dinosaurs. Their reasoning is that flight is most likely to have started from a tree-climbing ancestor, yet all the proposed dinosaurian ancestors were ground-dwellers. But the dino-bird supporters contend that an unknown dinosaurian bird-ancestor could have been tree-dwelling, or that birds evolved flight from the ground up by chasing and leaping after insects. Most of Feduccia and Martin's case against the 'birds-are-dinosaurs' hypothesis is based on differences between birds and dinosaurs. Supporters of cladistics, however, maintain that differences between organisms do not matter, as it is the similarities between them that count. Evolution dictates that organisms will change through time, so it is only the features which persist that carry useful information about their origins.

Most people on either side of the debate do accept, however, that the ancient winged creature known as Archaeopteryx is an ancestor of today’s birds. This is in spite of the fact that its form is distinctly non-bird-like, with a long bony tail, and teeth instead of a beak. The 'birds-are-dinosaurs' supporters contend that, if clearly-preserved feathers had not been found alongside two of the seven Archaeopteryx specimens, it would probably have been identified as a small dinosaur. However, Archaeopteryx does have some bird-like features, such as a furcula and bird-like feet, that suggest that it is too bird-like to be considered a dinosaur.

Over the last few decades several dinosaurs with bird-like features and primitive birds with dinosaur-like features have been found in several countries, connecting Archaeopteryx back to dinosaurs, and forwards to modern birds. Sinosauropteryx, excavated from 130-million-year-old rocks in northeast China, is one example. It has a dinosaur skeleton surrounded by a halo of fuzz, thought to be primitive feathers. And a reassessment of other dinosaurs reveals such bird-like features as hollow bones and a foot with three functional toes, characteristics that appeared over 50 million years before Archaeopteryx took to the air. And Rahonavis, a primitive bird from Madagascar is more bird-like than Archaeopteryx, yet retains some distinctive dinosaur features, including a long and vicious claw at the end of its wing. Over a century since Huxley's discovery, it seems that cladistics may have finally settled the 'dino-bird' debate.

questions.prompt: Feduccia and Martin believe that the ancestor of today’s birds was a kind of early ________ .
questions.evidence: They contend that birds evolved from some unknown reptile at a time long before dinosaurs.
questions.explanation: 题干问Feduccia和Martin，Their/They回指两位反对者；unknown reptile才是他们主张的祖先，不是另一阵营的dinosaur。

questions.prompt: In cladistics, the ________ between organisms’ characteristics are of major importance.
questions.evidence: it is the similarities between them that count.
questions.explanation: of major importance对应that count；differences do not matter是被否定项，不能只看到differences多次出现就选择。

questions.explanation: dangerous对应vicious，Madagascar锁定Rahonavis；claw位于翼末，不能错拿上一段Archaeopteryx的tail或teeth。

structure: 材料先交代不同阵营用什么解释飞行起源、看重哪些骨骼特征，再讨论兼有不同特征的化石，最后说明新增发现怎样连接更长的演化链。结尾仍保留seems和may，属于材料当时视角下的判断，不把它改写为无需条件的定论。
5：第5段介绍反对者的树栖起源推理，以及支持者提出的树栖恐龙或地面追逐昆虫的可能解释。随后争论转向比较依据：反对者强调差异，支序分类法的支持者在文中强调保留下来的共同特征。could和most likely表明这里包含假设与可能性，不能把任何一幅起源场景写成已直接观察到的过程。
6：第6段写双方多数人承认始祖鸟与现代鸟类有祖先关系，同时列举长骨尾、牙齿与鸟样足部、叉骨等混合特征。羽毛保存状况影响了人们如何识别标本。文中以这些特征讨论归类边界，不能只看名字中的“鸟”就忽略其复杂性。
7：第7段沿两个方向补充过渡联系：一端是带鸟样特征的恐龙，另一端是仍保留恐龙特征的早期鸟类。中华龙鸟周围的绒状物在文中被认为可能是原始羽毛；Rahonavis则展示更接近鸟类却仍有独特爪子的组合。结尾的谨慎语气与前面持续积累的证据相呼应。

phrases.meaning: 两位积极公开反对的人
phrases.explanation: vocal在此指公开、强烈地表达意见，不是专指嗓音特征。
persist强调特征经过时间仍然存在；which从句限定哪些特征承载相关信息。

phrases.phrase: in spite of the fact that
phrases.explanation: 引出完整从句，与前面的判断形成让步关系；不表示后面的事实被否认。
thought to be保留解释归属和不确定性，不能直接删去而写成毫无保留的鉴定。

sentences.text: The 'birds-are-dinosaurs' supporters contend that, if clearly-preserved feathers had not been found alongside two of the seven Archaeopteryx specimens, it would probably have been identified as a small dinosaur.
sentences.translation: 支持“鸟类源自恐龙”观点的人认为，如果七个始祖鸟标本中的两个旁边没有发现保存清晰的羽毛，它很可能就会被认作一种小型恐龙。

sentences.text: Over the last few decades several dinosaurs with bird-like features and primitive birds with dinosaur-like features have been found in several countries, connecting Archaeopteryx back to dinosaurs, and forwards to modern birds.
sentences.translation: 在此前几十年间，人们在几个国家发现了多种具有鸟样特征的恐龙，以及保留恐龙样特征的原始鸟类；这些发现把始祖鸟与更早的恐龙及更晚的现代鸟类联系起来。
sentences.explanation: 两个并列名词组dinosaurs with...与primitive birds with...共同作主语；have been found强调发现。connecting...补充这些发现形成的联系，back和forwards描述演化联系的两个方向，不是说始祖鸟个体向两个方向变化。

cases.title: 健康观念变化：年份、十年与三大领域

source.title: Cambridge IELTS Academic Reading Task Type 11 · Changing our Understanding of Health
source.originalUnit: Cambridge IELTS Academic Reading Task Type 11 · Changing our Understanding of Health
source.scope: 原出版社Academic短答worksheet及原答案；非自编题，也非完整考场试卷。

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: In the late 1940s the World Health Organisation challenged this physically and medically oriented view of health. They stated that "health is a complete state of physical, mental and social well-being and is not merely the absence of disease" (WHO, 1946). Health and the person were seen more holistically (mind/body/spirit) and not just in physical terms.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The 1970s was a time of focusing on the prevention of disease and illness by emphasising the importance of the lifestyle and behaviour of the individual. Specific behaviours which were seen to increase risk of disease, such as smoking, lack of fitness and unhealthy eating habits, were targeted. Creating health meant providing not only medical health care, but health promotion programs and policies which would help people maintain healthy behaviours and lifestyles. While this individualistic healthy lifestyles approach to health worked for some (the wealthy members of society), people experiencing poverty, unemployment, underemployment or little control over the conditions of their daily lives benefited little from this approach. This was largely because both the healthy lifestyles approach and the medical approach to health largely ignored the social and environmental conditions affecting the health of people.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: During the 1980s and 1990s there has been a growing swing away from seeing lifestyle risks as the root cause of poor health. While lifestyle factors still remain important, health is being viewed also in terms of the social, economic and environmental contexts in which people live. This broad approach to health is called the socio-ecological view of health. The broad socio-ecological view of health was endorsed at the first International Conference of Health Promotion held in 1986, Ottawa, Canada, where people from 38 countries agreed and declared that: "The fundamental conditions and resources for health are peace, shelter, education, food, a viable income, a stable eco-system, sustainable resources, social justice and equity. Improvement in health requires a secure foundation in these basic requirements." (WHO, 1986) It is clear from this statement that the creation of health is about much more than encouraging healthy individual behaviours and lifestyles and providing appropriate medical care. Therefore, the creation of health must include addressing issues such as poverty, pollution, urbanisation, natural resource depletion, social alienation and poor working conditions. The social, economic and environmental contexts which contribute to the creation of heath do not operate separately or independently of each other. Rather, they are interacting and interdependent, and it is the complex interrelationships between them which determine the conditions that promote health. A broad socio-ecological view of health suggests that the promotion of health must include a strong social, economic and environmental focus.

cases.instructions: Answer the questions below using NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer. Write your answers in boxes 1–3 on your answer sheet.

questions.prompt: In which year did the World Health Organisation define health in terms of mental, physical and social well-being?
questions.explanation: in which year要精确年份1946，不是笼统late 1940s。完整定义用于定位。

questions.prompt: Name the three broad areas which relate to people's health, according to the socio-ecological view of health.
questions.evidence: the social, economic and environmental contexts in which people live.
questions.explanation: socio-ecological锁定E段，不能抄C段physical, mental, social。只列三个词，不额外加contexts。

questions.prompt: During which decade were lifestyle risks seen as the major contributors to poor health?
questions.evidence: The 1970s was a time of focusing on the prevention of disease and illness by emphasising the importance of the lifestyle and behaviour of the individual.
questions.explanation: 问十年阶段，1970s强调个体生活方式；1980s/1990s已转向更广条件，不能误取转向时间。

structure: 三段展示健康观念在材料中的历史扩展：从身体疾病扩展到身心与社会福祉，再从个人行为扩展到人们所处的社会、经济与环境条件。后一种视角补充个人行为和医疗的不足，并未说这些因素不再重要。
C：C段引述世界卫生组织的健康定义，把健康理解为身体、心理、社会层面的整体福祉，而不仅是没有疾病。were seen和引文年份使这一段具有观念史性质；mind/body/spirit说明整体看待人的取向，不是在提供针对某种疾病的治疗方案。
D：D段叙述七十年代重视预防与个人生活方式的取向，包括吸烟、缺乏运动和饮食习惯。文中指出这种方式对不同群体的帮助并不相等：贫困、工作不稳定或难以控制生活条件的人受益有限。问题并非这些人不愿健康，而是方案忽略了影响选择的社会和环境条件。
E：E段进一步解释社会生态视角，把收入、住房、教育、资源与公平等纳入健康基础。While lifestyle factors still remain important明确保留生活方式的重要性。末尾强调社会、经济、环境条件彼此作用，不是把它们当成三项互不相关的清单；因此促进健康需要同时考虑这些联系。

phrases.phrase: not merely the absence of disease
phrases.explanation: not merely扩展定义而不是否定前项：没有疾病仍相关，但不是对健康的完整说明。

phrases.meaning: 维持有益健康的行为和生活方式
phrases.explanation: maintain强调持续维持；原文同时提醒，个人维持行为的能力受生活条件影响。
conditions在此是人生活的处境与条件，不是合同条款；需说清具体指收入、可达性或周边环境中的哪些因素。

phrases.meaning: 相互作用并且相互依赖
phrases.explanation: 两个并列形容词说明因素间的关系；不是各因素可以分别处理而互不影响。

sentences.text: While this individualistic healthy lifestyles approach to health worked for some (the wealthy members of society), people experiencing poverty, unemployment, underemployment or little control over the conditions of their daily lives benefited little from this approach.
sentences.translation: 虽然这种以个人健康生活方式为中心的做法对一些人——社会中的富裕成员——有效，但经历贫困、失业、就业不足，或很难掌控日常生活条件的人，从中获益很少。
sentences.explanation: While引出让步，worked for some限制受益范围；people后面的experiencing...修饰处于多种不利处境的人。little指获益很少，不等于严格意义上的零收益；this approach回指强调个人生活方式的取向。

sentences.text: Rather, they are interacting and interdependent, and it is the complex interrelationships between them which determine the conditions that promote health.
sentences.translation: 相反，这些条件彼此作用、相互依赖，决定有利于健康的条件的，是它们之间复杂的相互关系。
sentences.explanation: Rather承接前一句，纠正把不同条件当作独立因素的理解；they和them指社会、经济与环境背景。it is...which...是强调结构，突出complex interrelationships，而不是只突出其中单个因素。
